unmapped_findings: Chemical composition (Table I, wt.%): Si 0.92, C 0.94, Mn 29.10, P 0.043, S 0.006, Mo 0.33, Al 8.28, Cu 0.09; Table IV refers to this heat as '0.94% Si, 0.043% P'.
After 10 h at 530°C, the APT carbon amplitude for the 0.043% P steel is 6.0 at.% (compared with 4.4 at.% for the 0.006% P steel).
The high-phosphorus (0.043% P) specimens exhibited short-range ordering (SRO) that took place during the quench and prior to spinodal decomposition.
Room-temperature Charpy V-notch impact energy for the 0.043% P steel aged 10 h at 530°C reads just above ~20 J/cm² from Figure 9 (no exact numeric labels printed).
Fracture of the aged 0.043% P, 0.94% Si specimen produced a dendritic pattern with cleavage along {100}.
The DFT of this sample (100 kJ/m²) is much lower than the 1.07% Si low-P specimens aged for similar times at 530°C (376 kJ/m²).
In the 530°C age-hardening curve (Fig. 2b, '1% Si' steel), the 0.043% P steel attains peak hardness near 380 BHN around 30 h.
